nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show heterogeneous Zn deposition morphologies including large dendrites, dense uniform HZFs, sparse uniform HZFs, and sparse nonuniform HZFs on plated Zn surfaces at 1 and 10 mA/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images show random regions collected on a plated Zn metal surface after plated at 1 and 10 mA/cm² for 1 h (Figures 4A and 4B).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peak intensity ratio R = I002: I101 of pristine Zn(002) is 1.72, while random regions on plated Zn(002) surface fluctuate from 0.8 to 1.72, reflecting ECO information rather than ECF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R of pristine Zn is nearly a constant number (1.72), whereas R for random regions collected from the plated Zn metal surface at 10 mA/cm² fluctuates widely, ranging from 0.8 to 1.72 (Figures 4C and S12B).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show new peaks at 9.5°, 19.1°, and 28.9° corresponding to (001)ZHS, (002)ZHS, and (003)ZHS faces after Zn foil soaking or cycling, confirming ZHS formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The new peaks at 9.5°, 19.1°, and 28.9° on XRD patterns of the Zn foil and Gr@Zn after soaked or cycled, corresponding to the (001)ZHS, (002)ZHS, and (003)ZHS faces of ZHS (Figure 8H).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct values during cycling: Gr@Zn (208 to 120 Ω), SP@Zn (802 to 334 Ω), nano-SiO2@Zn (559 to 137 Ω), sand@Zn (2562 to 805 Ω), demonstrating coatings accelerate Zn²⁺ to Zn⁰ reduction except sand coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Rct of Zn/Zn cells before the cycle and after 10, 20, and 40 cycles present a decreased trend. The Rct values of sand@Zn, SP@Zn, nano-SiO2@Zn, and Gr@Zn during cycles are from 2,562 to 805, 802 to 334, 559 to 137, and 208 to 120 Ω, respectively (Figures 6E, 6F, and S21; Table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV-derived Zn²⁺ diffusion coefficients in initial three cycles: sand@Zn (0.03×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), SP@Zn (0.10×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), bare Zn (0.26×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), Gr@Zn (0.34×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), nano-SiO2@Zn (0.35×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), indicating nano-SiO2 and Gr promote faster mass transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The orders of average D in the initial three cycles from small to large are sand@Zn (0.03×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), SP@Zn (0.10×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), bare Zn (0.26×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), Gr@Zn (0.34×10⁻⁵ cm²/s), and nano-SiO2@Zn (0.35×10⁻⁵ cm²/s) (Figures 6C, 6D, and S20; Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electric double layer capacitance Cdl measurement shows ECSA of Gr@Zn is 7 times that of bare Zn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By measuring the electric double layer capacitance (Cdl) at non-faradaic region, we obtain the ECSA of conductive Gr@Zn is nearly 7 times that of bare Zn (Figures 7D and S25).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms ZnO composition on Zn foil soaked in deionized water and Zn hydroxides/zincates on Cu foil soaked in 1 M ZnSO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with relatively smooth vertical stripes of the pristine Zn foil (Figure 8B), the Zn foil after being soaked in deionized water displays dense spherical particles... and the main composition is ZnO (demonstrated by the energy dispersive X-ray spectrometer [EDS] and ex situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy [FTIR] in Figures S26B and S32).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ FTIR confirms ZnO on soaked Zn foil and ZHS formation on soaked samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FTIR and EDS results can further prove the formation of ZHS (Figures S29–S32).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of plated Zn on Zn(002), Zn(101), and Cu(200) substrates show preferred ECOs of [002]Zn, [101]Zn, and [101]Zn respectively, with peak intensity ratio R = I002:I101 changing from 1.72 to 1.27 for Zn(002), 0.5 to 0.25 for Zn(101), and 0 to 0.31 for Cu(200).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3I shows the XRD results of three substrates before and after plated Zn, the preferred ECO of plated Zn on Zn(002), Zn(101), and Cu(200) substrates are [002]Zn, [101]Zn, and [101]Zn, respectively... Figure 3J shows the peak intensity ratio between (002)Zn and (101)Zn (denoted as R = I002: I101) before and after deposition.
